sections.title: What Is llama.cpp?
sections.body: > **llama.cpp is a C/C++ implementation of LLM inference, written by Georgi Gerganov. It runs quantized GGUF models on virtually any hardware — CPU, NVIDIA GPU, AMD GPU, Apple Silicon (Metal), Vulkan — with extraordinary efficiency and zero Python dependencies.**

sections.title: llama.cpp Architecture
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              llama.cpp INTERNAL ARCHITECTURE                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  CORE DESIGN PRINCIPLES:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  1. Zero Python / PyTorch dependency
  2. Memory-mapped file I/O (fast load, low RAM usage)
  3. Hand-optimized SIMD kernels (AVX2, AVX512, NEON)
  4. Quantized computation kernels (not just storage!)
  5. Supports all major hardware backends

  BACKEND SUPPORT:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  CPU (all platforms):                                    │
  │    AVX/AVX2/AVX512    → Intel/AMD x86-64 optimization   │
  │    ARM NEON/SVE       → ARM CPU optimization             │
  │    OpenBLAS/BLAS      → Matrix multiply acceleration     │
  │                                                          │
  │  NVIDIA GPU:                                             │
  │    CUDA backend       → Full GPU acceleration            │
  │    cublas             → GPU matrix operations            │
  │    Flash Attention    → Efficient attention computation  │
  │                                                          │
  │  AMD GPU:                                                │
  │    ROCm/HIP backend   → AMD GPU support                  │
  │                                                          │
  │  Apple Silicon:                                          │
  │    Metal backend      → M1/M2/M3/M4 GPU acceleration     │
  │    Uses unified memory → GPU and CPU share memory!       │
  │                                                          │
  │  Others:                                                 │
  │    Vulkan             → Cross-platform GPU               │
  │    SYCL               → Intel GPU                        │
  │    OpenCL             → General GPU                      │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  HOW GPU OFFLOADING WORKS (n_gpu_layers):
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  LLaMA-3 8B has 32 transformer layers.

  n_gpu_layers=0:   ALL on CPU
  ┌─────────┐
  │ Layer 0 │ CPU
  │ Layer 1 │ CPU
  │   ...   │ CPU
  │Layer 31 │ CPU
  └─────────┘
  Speed: slowest (~5-10 tokens/sec on good CPU)

  n_gpu_layers=16:  HALF on GPU, half on CPU
  ┌─────────┐
  │ Layer 0 │ GPU ← fast
  │ ...     │ GPU
  │Layer 15 │ GPU
  ├─────────┤
  │Layer 16 │ CPU ← slower
  │ ...     │ CPU
  │Layer 31 │ CPU
  └─────────┘
  Speed: medium (~20-40 tokens/sec)

  n_gpu_layers=-1:  ALL on GPU
  ┌─────────┐
  │ Layer 0 │ GPU ← all fast
  │ ...     │ GPU
  │Layer 31 │ GPU
  └─────────┘
  Speed: fastest (~50-100+ tokens/sec)

  SPLIT MODE (multi-GPU):
  Layer 0-15:  GPU 0
  Layer 16-31: GPU 1
  Tensor parallel across GPUs!

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  KV CACHE — THE KEY TO FAST GENERATION:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  During generation, attention needs K and V for ALL past tokens.
  Without cache: recompute all past tokens EVERY step → O(n²)
  With KV cache: store K,V → just compute new token → O(n)

  KV cache size = 2 × layers × heads × head_dim × seq_len × dtype
  For LLaMA-3 8B, seq=4096: ~2 GB of KV cache needed!

  llama.cpp KV cache options:
  --ctx-size 4096    ← context length (= KV cache size)
  --cache-type-k q8_0 ← quantize K cache to save memory!
  --cache-type-v q8_0 ← quantize V cache to save memory!

  Quantized KV cache: 4x smaller, minimal quality loss ✅
```

# 💻 Complete Code — HuggingFace + GGUF + llama.cpp

```python name=hf_gguf_llamacpp/huggingface_complete.py
"""
HUGGINGFACE — Complete guide to every operation.
Loading models, tokenizing, generating, managing cache.
"""
import os, torch, json
from pathlib import Path
from transformers import (
    AutoTokenizer,
    AutoModelForCausalLM,
    pipeline,
    TextStreamer,
    TextIteratorStreamer,
    BitsAndBytesConfig,
    GenerationConfig,
)
from huggingface_hub import (
    hf_hub_download,
    snapshot_download,
    login,
    HfApi,
    list_models,
)
import threading

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1. AUTHENTICATION
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def authenticate_hf(token: str = None):
    """
    Authenticate with HuggingFace Hub.
    Required for gated models (LLaMA, Gemma, etc.)

    Get token: https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens
    Set scopes: Read access to your repos
    """
    token = token or os.getenv("HF_TOKEN") or os.getenv("HUGGINGFACE_HUB_TOKEN")

    if not token:
        raise ValueError(
            "No HF token found. Set HF_TOKEN env var or pass token."
            "\nGet token at: https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens"
        )

    login(token=token)
    print("  ✅ HuggingFace authentication successful")

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2. DOWNLOADING MODELS
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def download_model(
    model_name:   str,
    cache_dir:    str  = None,
    local_dir:    str  = None,
    ignore_patterns: list = None,
):
    """
    Download a model from HuggingFace Hub.

    cache_dir:  ~/.cache/huggingface/hub (default)
                Models cached here are reused automatically.

    local_dir:  Download to specific directory (no cache)

    ignore_patterns: Skip certain files
        ["*.bin"] → skip old PyTorch format
        ["*.gguf"] → skip GGUF files (if any)
        ["consolidated.*"] → skip large consolidated files
    """
    print(f"  Downloading: {model_name}")

    if ignore_patterns is None:
        # Download safetensors, skip old .bin format
        ignore_patterns = ["*.bin", "original/*"]

    path = snapshot_download(
        repo_id         = model_name,
        cache_dir       = cache_dir,
        local_dir       = local_dir,
        ignore_patterns = ignore_patterns,
    )

    # Show what was downloaded
    total_size = sum(
        f.stat().st_size
        for f in Path(path).rglob("*")
        if f.is_file()
    )
    print(f"  ✅ Downloaded to: {path}")
    print(f"  Total size: {total_size / 1e9:.2f} GB")
    return path

def download_single_file(
    repo_id:   str,
    filename:  str,
    local_dir: str = "./models",
):
    """
    Download a single file (e.g., one GGUF shard).
    """
    path = hf_hub_download(
        repo_id   = repo_id,
        filename  = filename,
        local_dir = local_dir,
    )
    size = Path(path).stat().st_size / 1e9
    print(f"  ✅ Downloaded: {filename} ({size:.2f} GB)")
    return path

def check_cache(model_name: str) -> dict:
    """
    Check if model is already in local cache.
    Returns cache info or None if not cached.
    """
    cache_dir  = Path.home() / ".cache" / "huggingface" / "hub"
    model_slug = "models--" + model_name.replace("/", "--")
    model_path = cache_dir / model_slug

    if model_path.exists():
        size = sum(
            f.stat().st_size
            for f in model_path.rglob("*")
            if f.is_file()
        )
        print(f"  ✅ Cached: {model_name} ({size/1e9:.2f} GB)")
        return {"cached": True, "path": str(model_path), "size_gb": size/1e9}
    else:
        print(f"  ❌ Not cached: {model_name}")
        return {"cached": False}

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3. LOADING MODELS — ALL CONFIGURATIONS
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def load_model_basic(model_name: str):
    """Load model in default FP16 — no quantization."""
    print(f"\n  Loading {model_name} in FP16...")

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model     = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_name,
        torch_dtype = torch.float16,
        device_map  = "auto",       # Automatically uses GPU if available
    )
    print(f"  ✅ Loaded. Device: {next(model.parameters()).device}")
    return model, tokenizer

def load_model_4bit(model_name: str):
    """Load model with 4-bit NF4 quantization (QLoRA-style)."""
    bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
        load_in_4bit              = True,
        bnb_4bit_quant_type       = "nf4",
        bnb_4bit_compute_dtype    = torch.bfloat16,
        bnb_4bit_use_double_quant = True,
    )
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model     = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_name,
        quantization_config = bnb_config,
        device_map          = "auto",
    )
    mem = torch.cuda.memory_allocated() / 1e9
    print(f"  ✅ 4-bit model loaded. GPU: {mem:.2f} GB")
    return model, tokenizer

def load_model_cpu(model_name: str):
    """Load model on CPU only — no GPU needed."""
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model     = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_name,
        torch_dtype = torch.float32,  # CPU prefers FP32
        device_map  = "cpu",
        low_cpu_mem_usage = True,     # Load layer by layer
    )
    print(f"  ✅ Model loaded on CPU")
    return model, tokenizer

def load_model_flash_attention(model_name: str):
    """Load with Flash Attention 2 — faster, longer context."""
    # pip install flash-attn --no-build-isolation
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model     = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_name,
        torch_dtype          = torch.bfloat16,
        device_map           = "auto",
        attn_implementation  = "flash_attention_2",  # Key!
    )
    print(f"  ✅ Flash Attention 2 model loaded")
    return model, tokenizer

def load_model_multi_gpu(model_name: str):
    """Load model split across multiple GPUs."""
    import json

    # Custom device map: split layers across GPUs
    # Auto device map does this automatically too
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model     = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_name,
        torch_dtype = torch.float16,
        device_map  = "auto",   # Splits across all available GPUs
        # OR manual split:
        # device_map = {
        #     "model.embed_tokens": 0,
        #     "model.layers.0-15": 0,   # First 16 layers on GPU 0
        #     "model.layers.16-31": 1,  # Last 16 layers on GPU 1
        #     "model.norm": 1,
        #     "lm_head": 1,
        # }
    )
    print(f"  ✅ Multi-GPU model loaded")
    print(f"  Device map: {model.hf_device_map}")
    return model, tokenizer

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4. TOKENIZATION — DEEP DIVE
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def tokenization_deep_dive(
    tokenizer,
    text: str,
):
    """
    Complete tokenization walkthrough.
    Shows every step of the process.
    """
    print(f"\n  Tokenizing: '{text}'")
    print(f"  {'─'*50}")

    # Basic tokenization
    tokens    = tokenizer.tokenize(text)
    token_ids = tokenizer.encode(text)
    decoded   = tokenizer.decode(token_ids)

    print(f"  Tokens:    {tokens}")
    print(f"  Token IDs: {token_ids}")
    print(f"  Decoded:   {decoded}")
    print(f"  Count:     {len(tokens)} tokens")

    # Token ID → string mapping
    print(f"\n  Token breakdown:")
    for tid in token_ids:
        token_str = tokenizer.decode([tid])
        print(f"    {tid:6d} → '{token_str}'")

    # Special tokens
    print(f"\n  Special tokens:")
    print(f"  BOS:   {tokenizer.bos_token} (id: {tokenizer.bos_token_id})")
    print(f"  EOS:   {tokenizer.eos_token} (id: {tokenizer.eos_token_id})")
    print(f"  PAD:   {tokenizer.pad_token} (id: {tokenizer.pad_token_id})")
    print(f"  UNK:   {tokenizer.unk_token} (id: {tokenizer.unk_token_id})")
    print(f"  Vocab: {tokenizer.vocab_size:,} tokens")

    # Chat template (for instruction models)
    if hasattr(tokenizer, "apply_chat_template"):
        messages = [
            {"role": "system",    "content": "You are helpful."},
            {"role": "user",      "content": text},
        ]
        formatted = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            messages,
            tokenize    = False,
            add_generation_prompt = True,
        )
        print(f"\n  Chat template applied:")
        print(f"  {formatted[:200]}...")

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 5. TEXT GENERATION — ALL METHODS
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def generate_basic(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    prompt:         str,
    max_new_tokens: int   = 200,
    temperature:    float = 0.7,
    top_p:          float = 0.9,
    do_sample:      bool  = True,
) -> str:
    """Standard text generation."""
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]

    # Apply chat template
    input_ids = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
        messages,
        return_tensors        = "pt",
        add_generation_prompt = True,
    ).to(model.device)

    with torch.no_grad():
        output = model.generate(
            input_ids,
            max_new_tokens  = max_new_tokens,
            do_sample       = do_sample,
            temperature     = temperature,
            top_p           = top_p,
            repetition_penalty = 1.1,
            pad_token_id    = tokenizer.eos_token_id,
        )

    # Decode only new tokens
    new_tokens = output[0][input_ids.shape[-1]:]
    return tokenizer.decode(new_tokens, skip_special_tokens=True)

def generate_streaming(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    prompt: str,
    max_new_tokens: int = 200,
):
    """
    Streaming generation — print tokens as they're generated.
    Like ChatGPT's streaming effect.
    """
    inputs = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
        [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        return_tensors        = "pt",
        add_generation_prompt = True,
    ).to(model.device)

    # TextStreamer: prints to stdout as tokens generate
    streamer = TextStreamer(
        tokenizer,
        skip_prompt            = True,  # Don't print the input
        skip_special_tokens    = True,
    )

    print("\n  Streaming: ", end="", flush=True)
    with torch.no_grad():
        model.generate(
            inputs,
            max_new_tokens = max_new_tokens,
            streamer       = streamer,
            do_sample      = True,
            temperature    = 0.7,
        )

def generate_streaming_thread(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    prompt: str,
    max_new_tokens: int = 200,
) -> str:
    """
    Streaming with TextIteratorStreamer.
    Use when you need to process tokens in a separate thread
    (e.g., web app, async code).
    """
    inputs   = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
        [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        return_tensors        = "pt",
        add_generation_prompt = True,
    ).to(model.device)

    streamer = TextIteratorStreamer(
        tokenizer,
        skip_prompt         = True,
        skip_special_tokens = True,
    )

    # Run generation in background thread
    gen_kwargs = dict(
        inputs,
        streamer       = streamer,
        max_new_tokens = max_new_tokens,
        do_sample      = True,
        temperature    = 0.7,
    )
    thread = threading.Thread(
        target=model.generate,
        kwargs=gen_kwargs,
    )
    thread.start()

    # Collect tokens as they arrive
    full_response = ""
    for new_text in streamer:
        full_response += new_text
        print(new_text, end="", flush=True)

    thread.join()
    return full_response

def generate_with_pipeline(
    model_name: str,
    prompts:    list[str],
):
    """
    High-level pipeline API.
    Best for batch processing.
    """
    pipe = pipeline(
        "text-generation",
        model               = model_name,
        torch_dtype         = torch.bfloat16,
        device_map          = "auto",
        model_kwargs        = {
            "attn_implementation": "flash_attention_2"
        },
    )

    results = pipe(
        prompts,
        max_new_tokens      = 200,
        do_sample           = True,
        temperature         = 0.7,
        return_full_text    = False,  # Only new tokens
        batch_size          = 4,
    )

    return [r[0]["generated_text"] for r in results]

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 6. UPLOADING TO HF HUB
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def upload_model_to_hub(
    model_path:     str,
    repo_id:        str,
    private:        bool = True,
    commit_message: str  = "Upload fine-tuned model",
):
    """
    Upload a model to HuggingFace Hub.
    Create repo at: https://huggingface.co/new
    """
    api = HfApi()

    # Create repo if doesn't exist
    api.create_repo(
        repo_id = repo_id,
        private = private,
        exist_ok= True,
    )

    # Upload all files in directory
    api.upload_folder(
        folder_path    = model_path,
        repo_id        = repo_id,
        commit_message = commit_message,
    )

    print(f"  ✅ Uploaded to: https://huggingface.co/{repo_id}")

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 7. SEARCH AND EXPLORE HF HUB
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def search_models(
    query:    str,
    task:     str  = None,
    library:  str  = None,
    limit:    int  = 10,
):
    """
    Search HuggingFace Hub for models.
    """
    api    = HfApi()
    models = api.list_models(
        search   = query,
        task     = task,       # "text-generation", "fill-mask", etc.
        library  = library,    # "transformers", "diffusers", etc.
        sort     = "downloads",
        direction= -1,
        limit    = limit,
    )

    print(f"\n  Search results for '{query}':")
    print(f"  {'─'*55}")
    for m in list(models)[:limit]:
        print(f"  {m.modelId:45s} ↓{m.downloads or 0:>8,}")

    return models
```

```python name=hf_gguf_llamacpp/gguf_complete.py
"""
GGUF — Complete guide: inspect, convert, quantize, manage.
"""
import struct, os, json
from pathlib import Path

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1. INSPECT GGUF FILES
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def inspect_gguf(file_path: str) -> dict:
    """
    Read and display all metadata from a GGUF file.
    No dependencies — pure Python binary reading.
    """
    GGUF_MAGIC   = 0x46554747  # "GGUF" in little-endian
    GGUF_VERSION = {1, 2, 3}

    # Value type IDs in GGUF
    GGUF_TYPE = {
        0:  ("uint8",  "B", 1),
        1:  ("int8",   "b", 1),
        2:  ("uint16", "H", 2),
        3:  ("int16",  "h", 2),
        4:  ("uint32", "I", 4),
        5:  ("int32",  "i", 4),
        6:  ("float32","f", 4),
        7:  ("bool",   "?", 1),
        8:  ("string", None, None),
        9:  ("array",  None, None),
        10: ("uint64", "Q", 8),
        11: ("int64",  "q", 8),
        12: ("float64","d", 8),
    }

    metadata = {}

    with open(file_path, "rb") as f:
        # Read and verify magic
        magic = struct.unpack("<I", f.read(4))[0]
        if magic != GGUF_MAGIC:
            raise ValueError(f"Not a GGUF file: {file_path}")

        version = struct.unpack("<I", f.read(4))[0]
        if version not in GGUF_VERSION:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown GGUF version: {version}")

        n_tensors = struct.unpack("<Q", f.read(8))[0]
        n_kv      = struct.unpack("<Q", f.read(8))[0]

        metadata["_gguf_version"] = version
        metadata["_n_tensors"]    = n_tensors
        metadata["_n_kv_pairs"]   = n_kv

        def read_string() -> str:
            length = struct.unpack("<Q", f.read(8))[0]
            return f.read(length).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

        def read_value(vtype: int):
            if vtype in GGUF_TYPE and GGUF_TYPE[vtype][1]:
                fmt, size = GGUF_TYPE[vtype][1], GGUF_TYPE[vtype][2]
                return struct.unpack(f"<{fmt}", f.read(size))[0]
            elif vtype == 8:  # string
                return read_string()
            elif vtype == 7:  # bool
                return bool(struct.unpack("<B", f.read(1))[0])
            elif vtype == 9:  # array
                arr_type  = struct.unpack("<I", f.read(4))[0]
                arr_count = struct.unpack("<Q", f.read(8))[0]
                items     = []
                for _ in range(min(arr_count, 5)):
                    items.append(read_value(arr_type))
                if arr_count > 5:
                    items.append(f"... ({arr_count - 5} more)")
                return items
            return None

        # Read all metadata key-value pairs
        for _ in range(n_kv):
            key   = read_string()
            vtype = struct.unpack("<I", f.read(4))[0]
            value = read_value(vtype)
            metadata[key] = value

    # Print summary
    arch   = metadata.get("general.architecture", "unknown")
    name   = metadata.get("general.name", "unknown")
    params = metadata.get(f"{arch}.block_count", "?")
    ctx    = metadata.get(f"{arch}.context_length", "?")
    emb    = metadata.get(f"{arch}.embedding_length", "?")
    ft     = metadata.get("general.file_type", "?")

    file_size = Path(file_path).stat().st_size / 1e9

    print(f"\n  📦 GGUF File: {Path(file_path).name}")
    print(f"  {'─'*50}")
    print(f"  Name:         {name}")
    print(f"  Architecture: {arch}")
    print(f"  Layers:       {params}")
    print(f"  Context:      {ctx} tokens")
    print(f"  Embedding:    {emb}")
    print(f"  File type:    {ft}")
    print(f"  Tensors:      {n_tensors:,}")
    print(f"  File size:    {file_size:.2f} GB")
    print(f"\n  Key metadata:")
    for k, v in sorted(metadata.items()):
        if not k.startswith("_") and not k.startswith("tokenizer"):
            print(f"  {k}: {str(v)[:60]}")

    return metadata

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2. CONVERT HF → GGUF
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def convert_hf_to_gguf(
    hf_model_path:  str,
    output_dir:     str,
    output_type:    str  = "f16",  # f16, f32, bf16, q8_0
    llama_cpp_dir:  str  = "./llama.cpp",
):
    """
    Convert HuggingFace model to GGUF format.

    Requirements:
    git clone https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp
    pip install -r llama.cpp/requirements.txt

    output_type options:
    f32  → FP32, largest, highest quality
    f16  → FP16, half size ← recommended for conversion
    bf16 → BF16, same size as f16
    q8_0 → 8-bit quantized directly

    NOTE: Usually convert to f16 first, then quantize with
    llama-quantize for more format options.
    """
    import subprocess
    from pathlib import Path

    os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
    model_name  = Path(hf_model_path).name
    output_file = Path(output_dir) / f"{model_name}-{output_type}.gguf"

    print(f"\n  Converting {hf_model_path} → GGUF {output_type}")

    cmd = [
        "python",
        f"{llama_cpp_dir}/convert_hf_to_gguf.py",
        hf_model_path,
        "--outtype",  output_type,
        "--outfile",  str(output_file),
        "--vocab-type", "bpe",   # or spm, unigram
    ]

    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        print(f"  ❌ Conversion failed:\n{result.stderr}")
        raise RuntimeError("Conversion failed")

    size = output_file.stat().st_size / 1e9
    print(f"  ✅ Converted: {output_file} ({size:.2f} GB)")
    return str(output_file)

def quantize_gguf(
    input_file:  str,
    output_file: str,
    quant_type:  str = "Q4_K_M",
    llama_cpp_dir: str = "./llama.cpp",
    imatrix_file:  str = None,  # For IQ quantization
):
    """
    Quantize a GGUF file (usually from F16) to target format.

    Standard quants (no imatrix needed):
    Q2_K, Q3_K_S, Q3_K_M, Q4_0, Q4_K_S, Q4_K_M,
    Q5_0, Q5_K_M, Q6_K, Q8_0

    Importance-matrix quants (better quality, need imatrix):
    IQ2_XXS, IQ2_XS, IQ3_XXS, IQ4_XS, IQ4_NL
    """
    import subprocess

    print(f"\n  Quantizing to {quant_type}...")
    print(f"  Input:  {input_file}")
    print(f"  Output: {output_file}")

    cmd = [f"{llama_cpp_dir}/llama-quantize"]

    if imatrix_file:
        cmd += ["--imatrix", imatrix_file]

    cmd += [input_file, output_file, quant_type]

    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        print(f"  ❌ Quantization failed:\n{result.stderr}")
        raise RuntimeError("Quantization failed")

    in_size  = Path(input_file).stat().st_size  / 1e9
    out_size = Path(output_file).stat().st_size / 1e9
    ratio    = out_size / in_size

    print(f"  ✅ Done! {in_size:.2f} GB → {out_size:.2f} GB "
          f"({ratio:.0%} of original)")
    return output_file

def generate_imatrix(
    input_gguf:  str,
    output_file: str = "imatrix.dat",
    calibration: str = None,
    llama_cpp_dir: str = "./llama.cpp",
):
    """
    Generate importance matrix for IQ quantization.
    Improves quality of IQ* quantization formats.

    calibration: Path to calibration text file.
    Uses wikitext-like data (~1MB of diverse text).
    """
    import subprocess

    if not calibration:
        # Create a simple calibration file
        calibration = "calibration.txt"
        with open(calibration, "w") as f:
            f.write("""
The transformer architecture was introduced in the paper
"Attention Is All You Need" by Vaswani et al. in 2017.
It consists of encoder and decoder blocks with self-attention
mechanisms. Large language models like GPT and LLaMA use the
decoder-only architecture for text generation tasks.
Machine learning models learn patterns from training data.
The optimization process uses gradient descent to minimize loss.
""" * 50)  # Repeat for more calibration data

    print(f"  Generating importance matrix from {input_gguf}...")

    cmd = [
        f"{llama_cpp_dir}/llama-imatrix",
        "-m",  input_gguf,
        "-f",  calibration,
        "-o",  output_file,
        "--chunk", "512",
        "-ngl", "0",  # CPU only for imatrix
    ]

    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode == 0:
        print(f"  ✅ imatrix saved: {output_file}")
    else:
        print(f"  ❌ imatrix failed: {result.stderr[:200]}")

    return output_file

def download_gguf_from_hub(
    repo_id:    str,
    filename:   str,
    local_dir:  str = "./models",
) -> str:
    """
    Download a specific GGUF file from HuggingFace.
    Most convenient way to get GGUF models.

    Popular repos:
    bartowski/*         → High quality quants, many models
    TheBloke/*          → Large collection (older style)
    unsloth/*           → Unsloth-optimized GGUF
    lmstudio-community/*→ LM Studio-tested quants
    """
    from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

    print(f"  Downloading {filename}")
    print(f"  From: {repo_id}")

    path = hf_hub_download(
        repo_id   = repo_id,
        filename  = filename,
        local_dir = local_dir,
    )

    size = Path(path).stat().st_size / 1e9
    print(f"  ✅ Downloaded: {path} ({size:.2f} GB)")
    return path

def batch_quantize_all_formats(
    f16_gguf:     str,
    output_dir:   str,
    formats:      list = None,
    llama_cpp_dir:str  = "./llama.cpp",
):
    """
    Create all quantization variants from one F16 GGUF.
    Useful when publishing model to HuggingFace.
    """
    if formats is None:
        formats = ["Q2_K", "Q3_K_M", "Q4_K_M", "Q5_K_M", "Q6_K", "Q8_0"]

    os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
    model_base = Path(f16_gguf).stem.replace("-f16", "")

    print(f"\n  Creating {len(formats)} quantized variants...")
    results = {}

    for fmt in formats:
        out_file = Path(output_dir) / f"{model_base}-{fmt}.gguf"
        try:
            quantize_gguf(f16_gguf, str(out_file), fmt, llama_cpp_dir)
            results[fmt] = {
                "path": str(out_file),
                "size_gb": out_file.stat().st_size / 1e9,
            }
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  ❌ {fmt} failed: {e}")
            results[fmt] = {"error": str(e)}

    # Summary table
    print(f"\n  {'Format':12s} {'Size':8s} {'vs F16':8s}")
    f16_size = Path(f16_gguf).stat().st_size / 1e9
    print(f"  {'F16':12s} {f16_size:6.2f} GB {'100%':>8s}")
    for fmt, info in results.items():
        if "size_gb" in info:
            ratio = info["size_gb"] / f16_size
            print(f"  {fmt:12s} {info['size_gb']:6.2f} GB {ratio:>7.0%}")

    return results

"""

import os, json, subprocess
from pathlib import Path

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1. BUILD llama.cpp
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def build_llamacpp(
    install_dir:   str  = "./llama.cpp",
    cuda:          bool = False,
    metal:         bool = False,  # macOS
    vulkan:        bool = False,
    opencl:        bool = False,
):
    """
    Clone and build llama.cpp from source.

    Automatically detects best backend for your system.
    """
    import platform

    # Auto-detect backend
    system = platform.system()
    if metal is None:
        metal  = system == "Darwin"  # macOS = use Metal
    if cuda is None:
        # Check for NVIDIA GPU
        try:
            subprocess.run(
                ["nvidia-smi"], capture_output=True, check=True
            )
            cuda = True
        except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError):
            cuda = False

    print(f"  Building llama.cpp:")
    print(f"  CUDA: {cuda} | Metal: {metal} | Vulkan: {vulkan}")

    # Clone
    if not Path(install_dir).exists():
        subprocess.run([
            "git", "clone",
            "https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp",
            install_dir,
        ], check=True)

    # Build with cmake
    build_dir = f"{install_dir}/build"
    os.makedirs(build_dir, exist_ok=True)

    cmake_args = [
        "cmake", "..",
        f"-DGGML_CUDA={'ON' if cuda else 'OFF'}",
        f"-DGGML_METAL={'ON' if metal else 'OFF'}",
        f"-DGGML_VULKAN={'ON' if vulkan else 'OFF'}",
        "-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release",
    ]

    subprocess.run(cmake_args, cwd=build_dir, check=True)
    subprocess.run(
        ["cmake", "--build", ".", "--config", "Release",
         "--parallel", str(os.cpu_count())],
        cwd=build_dir, check=True,
    )

    print(f"  ✅ llama.cpp built at {install_dir}")
    return install_dir

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2. RUN INFERENCE WITH llama-cli
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def run_llamacpp_cli(
    model_path:      str,
    prompt:          str,
    n_predict:       int   = 200,
    n_ctx:           int   = 4096,
    n_gpu_layers:    int   = -1,   # -1 = all layers on GPU
    temperature:     float = 0.7,
    top_p:           float = 0.9,
    top_k:           int   = 40,
    repeat_penalty:  float = 1.1,
    n_threads:       int   = None, # None = auto
    chat_mode:       bool  = True,
    system_prompt:   str   = "You are a helpful assistant.",
    llama_cpp_dir:   str   = "./llama.cpp",
) -> str:
    """
    Run llama.cpp CLI inference.
    Full control over all parameters.
    """
    n_threads = n_threads or max(1, os.cpu_count() // 2)

    # Build command
    cli_path = (
        f"{llama_cpp_dir}/build/bin/llama-cli"
        if Path(f"{llama_cpp_dir}/build/bin/llama-cli").exists()
        else f"{llama_cpp_dir}/llama-cli"
    )

    cmd = [
        cli_path,
        "--model",           model_path,
        "--predict",         str(n_predict),
        "--ctx-size",        str(n_ctx),
        "--n-gpu-layers",    str(n_gpu_layers),
        "--temp",            str(temperature),
        "--top-p",           str(top_p),
        "--top-k",           str(top_k),
        "--repeat-penalty",  str(repeat_penalty),
        "--threads",         str(n_threads),
        "--no-display-prompt",
        "--log-disable",
    ]

    if chat_mode:
        cmd += [
            "--chat-template",  "llama3",  # or chatml, mistral, etc.
            "--system-prompt",  system_prompt,
            "--prompt",         f"[INST]{prompt}[/INST]",
            "--in-prefix",      " [INST] ",
            "--in-suffix",      " [/INST]",
        ]
    else:
        cmd += ["--prompt", prompt]

    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        print(f"  ❌ Error: {result.stderr[:200]}")
        return ""

    return result.stdout.strip()

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3. llama-server (OpenAI-compatible API)
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def start_llama_server(
    model_path:     str,
    host:           str  = "0.0.0.0",
    port:           int  = 8080,
    n_ctx:          int  = 4096,
    n_gpu_layers:   int  = -1,
    n_parallel:     int  = 4,      # Parallel inference slots
    n_threads:      int  = None,
    api_key:        str  = None,
    llama_cpp_dir:  str  = "./llama.cpp",
) -> subprocess.Popen:
    """
    Start llama-server: OpenAI-compatible HTTP server.

    Endpoints available:
    GET  /health                 → Server health check
    POST /v1/chat/completions    → OpenAI-compatible chat
    POST /v1/completions         → Text completion
    POST /v1/embeddings          → Embeddings
    GET  /v1/models              → List models
    POST /tokenize               → Tokenize text
    POST /detokenize             → Detokenize tokens
    GET  /metrics                → Prometheus metrics
    """
    n_threads = n_threads or max(1, os.cpu_count() // 2)

    server_path = (
        f"{llama_cpp_dir}/build/bin/llama-server"
        if Path(f"{llama_cpp_dir}/build/bin/llama-server").exists()
        else f"{llama_cpp_dir}/llama-server"
    )

    cmd = [
        server_path,
        "--model",          model_path,
        "--host",           host,
        "--port",           str(port),
        "--ctx-size",       str(n_ctx),
        "--n-gpu-layers",   str(n_gpu_layers),
        "--parallel",       str(n_parallel),
        "--threads",        str(n_threads),
        "--cont-batching",              # Continuous batching
        "--flash-attn",                 # Flash attention
        "--cache-type-k", "q8_0",       # Quantize KV cache
        "--cache-type-v", "q8_0",
    ]

    if api_key:
        cmd += ["--api-key", api_key]

    print(f"\n  Starting llama-server...")
    print(f"  Model: {model_path}")
    print(f"  URL:   http://{host}:{port}")
    print(f"  API:   http://{host}:{port}/v1/chat/completions")

    process = subprocess.Popen(
        cmd,
        stdout = subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr = subprocess.PIPE,
    )

    # Wait for server to be ready
    import time, urllib.request
    for attempt in range(30):
        time.sleep(1)
        try:
            urllib.request.urlopen(
                f"http://localhost:{port}/health",
                timeout=2,
            )
            print(f"  ✅ Server ready on port {port}")
            break
        except Exception:
            if attempt == 29:
                print(f"  ❌ Server failed to start")
            continue

    return process

def query_llama_server(
    prompt:     str,
    host:       str   = "localhost",
    port:       int   = 8080,
    model:      str   = "local-model",
    max_tokens: int   = 200,
    temperature:float = 0.7,
    stream:     bool  = False,
    api_key:    str   = None,
) -> str:
    """
    Query llama-server using OpenAI SDK.
    Works identically to OpenAI API!
    """
    from openai import OpenAI

    client = OpenAI(
        base_url = f"http://{host}:{port}/v1",
        api_key  = api_key or "not-needed",  # Required by SDK
    )

    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model    = model,
        messages = [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        max_tokens  = max_tokens,
        temperature = temperature,
        stream      = stream,
    )

    if stream:
        full = ""
        for chunk in response:
            delta = chunk.choices[0].delta.content or ""
            full += delta
            print(delta, end="", flush=True)
        return full
    else:
        return response.choices[0].message.content

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4. PYTHON API (llama-cpp-python)
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def llamacpp_python_complete(
    model_path:    str,
    prompt:        str,
    n_gpu_layers:  int   = -1,
    n_ctx:         int   = 4096,
    max_tokens:    int   = 200,
    temperature:   float = 0.7,
    stream:        bool  = False,
):
    """
    Use llama-cpp-python for inference.

    Install:
    # CPU only:
    pip install llama-cpp-python

    # CUDA:
    CMAKE_ARGS="-DGGML_CUDA=on" pip install llama-cpp-python

    # Metal (macOS):
    CMAKE_ARGS="-DGGML_METAL=on" pip install llama-cpp-python

    # Vulkan:
    CMAKE_ARGS="-DGGML_VULKAN=on" pip install llama-cpp-python
    """
    from llama_cpp import Llama, LlamaGrammar

    print(f"\n  Loading model: {model_path}")

    llm = Llama(
        model_path    = model_path,
        n_gpu_layers  = n_gpu_layers,  # -1 = all on GPU
        n_ctx         = n_ctx,
        n_threads     = os.cpu_count() // 2,
        n_batch       = 512,           # Prompt processing batch
        use_mmap      = True,          # Memory-mapped I/O
        use_mlock     = False,         # Lock in RAM (prevents swap)
        verbose       = False,
        # Flash attention:
        # flash_attn  = True,          # Requires build support
    )

    print(f"  ✅ Model loaded")

    # ── Chat completion (OpenAI-compatible) ───────────
    messages = [
        {"role": "system",  "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
        {"role": "user",    "content": prompt},
    ]

    if stream:
        print(f"  Streaming response: ", end="", flush=True)
        response_text = ""
        for chunk in llm.create_chat_completion(
            messages    = messages,
            max_tokens  = max_tokens,
            temperature = temperature,
            stream      = True,
        ):
            delta = chunk["choices"][0]["delta"].get("content", "")
            response_text += delta
            print(delta, end="", flush=True)
        print()
        return response_text
    else:
        response = llm.create_chat_completion(
            messages    = messages,
            max_tokens  = max_tokens,
            temperature = temperature,
        )
        return response["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]

def llamacpp_embeddings(
    model_path: str,
    texts:      list[str],
) -> list[list[float]]:
    """
    Generate embeddings with llama.cpp.
    Use an embedding-specific model for best results:
    nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5-GGUF
    """
    from llama_cpp import Llama

    llm = Llama(
        model_path   = model_path,
        embedding    = True,          # Enable embedding mode!
        n_gpu_layers = -1,
        n_ctx        = 512,
        verbose      = False,
    )

    embeddings = []
    for text in texts:
        result = llm.create_embedding(text)
        emb    = result["data"][0]["embedding"]
        embeddings.append(emb)

    print(f"  ✅ Generated {len(embeddings)} embeddings, "
          f"dim={len(embeddings[0])}")
    return embeddings

def benchmark_model(
    model_path:   str,
    llama_cpp_dir:str  = "./llama.cpp",

) -> dict:
    """

    bench_path = (

        if Path(f"{llama_cpp_dir}/build/bin/llama-bench").exists()
        else f"{llama_cpp_dir}/llama-bench"

    result = subprocess.run([
        bench_path,
        "-m",    model_path,
        "-ngl",  str(n_gpu_layers),
        "-p",    "512",   # Prompt tokens
        "-n",    "128",   # Generated tokens
        "-r",    "3",     # Repetitions
        "--output", "json",
    ], capture_output=True, text=True)

    if result.returncode == 0:
        try:
            data = json.loads(result.stdout)
            print(f"\n  Benchmark results:")
            for r in data.get("results", []):
                print(f"  Prompt: {r.get('t_p','?'):.1f} ms | "
                      f"Gen: {r.get('t_g','?'):.1f} ms | "
                      f"Speed: {r.get('speed','?'):.1f} tok/s")
            return data
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            print(f"  Raw output: {result.stdout[:200]}")
    return {}

def demo_compare_quantizations():
    """
    Compare quality across quantization levels.
    Shows the quality/size tradeoff visually.
    """
    from hf_gguf_llamacpp.llamacpp_complete import llamacpp_python_complete
    from hf_gguf_llamacpp.gguf_complete import download_gguf_from_hub
    from pathlib import Path

    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("DEMO 3: Quality Comparison Across Quants")
    print("="*60)

    quant_files = {
        "Q2_K":   "Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-Q2_K.gguf",
        "Q4_K_M": "Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf",
        "Q6_K":   "Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-Q6_K.gguf",
        "Q8_0":   "Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-Q8_0.gguf",
    }

    test_prompt = "Explain quantum entanglement in simple terms."
    results     = {}

    for quant_name, filename in quant_files.items():
        model_path = f"./models/{filename}"

        if not Path(model_path).exists():
            print(f"  Skipping {quant_name} (not downloaded)")
            continue

        size_gb = Path(model_path).stat().st_size / 1e9
        response = llamacpp_python_complete(
            model_path   = model_path,
            prompt       = test_prompt,
            n_gpu_layers = 0,
            max_tokens   = 150,
            temperature  = 0.0,  # Deterministic for comparison
        )
        results[quant_name] = {
            "size_gb":  size_gb,
            "response": response,
        }

    print(f"\n  {'Quant':10s} {'Size':8s} {'Response preview'}")
    print(f"  {'─'*70}")
    for quant, data in results.items():
        preview = data["response"][:60].replace("\n", " ")
        print(f"  {quant:10s} {data['size_gb']:.2f} GB  {preview}...")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Run demos
    demo_download_and_run_gguf()
    # demo_hf_to_gguf_pipeline()
    # demo_compare_quantizations()
```

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         HUGGINGFACE + GGUF + llama.cpp COMPLETE SUMMARY          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  THE THREE PILLARS:
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  HuggingFace   = Where models LIVE, TRAINED, and SHARED
  GGUF          = How models are PACKAGED for portability
  llama.cpp     = How models are RUN anywhere

  WHEN TO USE WHAT:
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ┌────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Scenario              │  Tool                                │
  ├────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤
  │  Fine-tuning a model   │  HuggingFace transformers + PEFT    │
  │  Using GPU (NVIDIA)    │  HuggingFace + bitsandbytes          │
  │  Running on CPU        │  GGUF + llama.cpp                    │
  │  Running on Mac        │  GGUF + llama.cpp (Metal)            │
  │  Running on mobile     │  GGUF (llama.cpp port)               │
  │  Building an API       │  llama-server (OpenAI-compatible)    │
  │  Quick prototyping     │  Ollama (wraps llama.cpp)            │
  │  Production serving    │  vLLM (GPU) or llama-server (CPU)   │
  │  Sharing your model    │  HuggingFace Hub                     │
  │  Finding models        │  HuggingFace Hub search              │
  └────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┘

  GGUF FORMAT CHEAT SHEET:
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Q2_K   → 2.6 bits → smallest → ⚠️ quality loss
  Q3_K_M → 3.4 bits → very small → acceptable
  Q4_K_M → 4.9 bits → sweet spot → ✅ recommended default
  Q5_K_M → 5.7 bits → high quality → use if RAM allows
  Q6_K   → 6.6 bits → excellent → near-lossless
  Q8_0   → 8.5 bits → best → ~identical to F16
  F16    → 16 bits  → full → exact copy

  llama.cpp QUICK COMMANDS:
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Run in terminal:
  ./llama-cli -m model.gguf -p "Hello!" -n 100

  # Start API server:
  ./llama-server -m model.gguf --port 8080

  # Quantize:
  ./llama-quantize model-f16.gguf model-Q4_K_M.gguf Q4_K_M

  # Benchmark:
  ./llama-bench -m model.gguf

  # Python API:
  from llama_cpp import Llama
  llm = Llama(model_path="model.gguf", n_gpu_layers=-1)
  print(llm("Hello!")["choices"][0]["text"])

  ECOSYSTEM TOOLS BUILT ON llama.cpp:
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Ollama     → CLI wrapper, model management, easy API
  LM Studio  → GUI app for running GGUF models
  GPT4All    → Desktop app with local models
  Jan        → Open-source ChatGPT alternative (local)
  Open WebUI → Web interface for llama-server/Ollama
  AnythingLLM→ Full RAG system with local models
```
